## Design

### 2026-10-11 – I worked on the whole Starbie project, from the electronics to the firmware. In KiCad 10, I designed the schematic and PCB around a Seeed XIAO ESP32-C3, a 0.96" I2C OLED display, an 8-pin header for a

**9h**

I worked on the whole Starbie project, from the electronics to the firmware. In KiCad 10, I designed the schematic and PCB around a Seeed XIAO ESP32-C3, a 0.96" I2C OLED display, an 8-pin header for an MPU6050 motion sensor, a DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor with a 10 kΩ pull-up resistor, and two Cherry MX buttons. I imported the custom footprints for the display and the XIAO, routed every net (I2C, DHT11, buttons, power and ground) across the front and back copper layers with vias, and drew and filled a GND copper zone on the back layer. The design rule check passes with no errors, only two library footprint warnings that don’t affect manufacturing, and all connections are routed. I then exported the Gerber files and drill files for fabrication. On the firmware side, I set up the Arduino IDE with the ESP32 board package and the Adafruit libraries, and I wrote the Starbie sketch for the XIAO_ESP32C3. It shows an animated pet on the OLED, a radial menu controlled by tilting the board, two buttons, a stats screen with temperature and humidity, a shake reaction, a sparkle effect and a custom 32x32 sprite. I checked that the code’s pin assignments match my board’s wiring, and the sketch compiles using about 25% of the program memory. Finally, I put the KiCad project, Gerbers and firmware in a GitHub repository, resolved a merge conflict and pushed it. I used Claude as an AI assistant for parts of the firmware, the documentation and troubleshooting. The project hasn’t been tested on assembled hardware yet.
